rationale: A wins because it keeps the facts on a leash and turns them into four real routes, especially "REI's record payout to members lands as workers organize at its stores," while still warning when not to pitch. B has useful instincts, but "REI won't say how big its resale business actually is, even as it leans on it for sustainability credit" turns an undisclosed number into a refusal and then pads the same rollout into "core retail infrastructure." That is how a smart angle starts dressing up a hole as a story.
gaps_in_A: "resale and repair stop being a side channel and become something every store has to staff and stock" overstates the facts. The update says trade-ins and repairs are available at every store; it does not say every store stocks used gear or has repair staff on site.

"test whether the co-op structure is producing different decisions than a public retailer would make" invites a comparative claim A otherwise wisely refuses. Without competitor evidence, keep this as a question, not a premise.

It throws away "REI's resale expansion advances its sustainability commitments" only as a duplicate. The real version is an accountability question around "share of sales from used gear not disclosed," which A mentions later but does not fully develop as an angle.
gaps_in_B: "REI won't say how big its resale business actually is" is too cute by half. "Not disclosed" is a gap; it is not proof REI refused to say.

"leans on it for sustainability credit" loads motive onto the facts. The update says REI says resale and repair support sustainability commitments; B turns that into prosecutorial framing before it has evidence.

"REI's bet: gear resale and repair aren't a sustainability side project, they're core retail infrastructure" is mostly a duplicate of the first rollout angle, just with a bigger hat. Same fact, inflated altitude.

"customer-story" paired with "A retail-ops or outdoor-industry trade reporter" cannot decide its protagonist. B also misses the clean local-store feature that becomes possible once every REI market has the program.
